consensus_summary: The blind consensus identifies grapes primarily as spiritual fruitfulness — the good fruit (righteousness, faithfulness) God expects from his covenant people pictured as a vine/vineyard, with wild/sour grapes marking apostasy. Well-established secondary strands: grapes of wrath crushed in the winepress of judgment (Rev 14; Isa 63), the abundance/blessing of the land (Num 13; Deut 8), the eucharistic 'fruit of the vine' as Christ's blood, and (in some responses) Israel/God's people themselves as the grapes (Hos 9:10; Ps 80).
book_summary: The book identifies grapes as a people's works ripened into persons — the persons themselves are the vineyard's yield — and holds that pressing the grapes yields either covenant wine or the blood of judgment depending on whether the vintage is good or wild.
consensus_core_identification: Grapes = the fruit (faithfulness/righteousness or its lack) God seeks from his covenant people, with contextual extensions to blessing, judgment in the winepress, and eucharistic blood.
book_core_identification: Grapes = persons produced by a people's collective works (the vineyard's human yield), whose pressing bifurcates into covenant wine (good vintage) or blood of judgment (wild vintage).
boundary_disagreement: The consensus generally treats grapes as abstract fruit/works or moral character, with 'people as grapes' listed only as a secondary alternative (Hos 9:10). The book fuses and sharpens these: works ripen into persons, so the yield is persons, not deeds. It also reclassifies the eucharistic-wine and wrath-blood strands: rather than two independent symbolic contexts, they become the two conditional outcomes of a single pressing, determined by vintage quality (good vs wild). The book excludes or at least sidelines the plain 'material abundance of the land' reading that Responses A, C, and D treat as common.
material_contradiction: None. The book's identification is a unification and precision of consensus strands, not a replacement of the central referent (the vineyard's yield expected from God's people).
rationale: Both readings center on the same image: the yield God seeks from his covenant vineyard, good versus wild grapes, and the winepress producing wine or judgment blood. The book preserves this referent but materially tightens it — grapes are persons ripened from a people's works (supported by Mic 7:1-2 where the missing cluster is the perished good man, Hos 9:10 where Israel is grapes, and Isa 65:8 where servants are preserved in the cluster), and the wine/blood outcomes are made conditional products of one pressing rather than separate motifs. This is a boundary-and-mechanism refinement within the consensus category, not a divergent replacement, and not novel since persons-as-grapes and both pressing outcomes appear among consensus alternatives.
strongest_objection: One could argue MATCH: the consensus already contains every element (fruitfulness, people-as-grapes, wine/Eucharist, winepress wrath), so the book merely restates the multivalent consensus in condensed form, and 'works ripened into persons' is poetic phrasing rather than a materially different identification. Conversely, one could argue the persons-as-yield claim shifts the referent from works to people strongly enough to press toward divergence; but Hos 9:10 and Mic 7:1-2 in the consensus responses already admit that identification.
